event.description: Repair legacy refs and test head-shared asymmetric bilinear attention
event.proposal: Family: attention organization. Current retained frontier is 1,672 parameters at 99.010000%, a +0.010000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 4 prior logged attempts in this family. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0020, which removed attention output projections and qualified at 3,168 parameters and 99.94%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0097, whose per-head symmetric bilinear substitution was a valid nonqualification at 1,481 parameters and 0.00%. The immediately preceding launch of this exact candidate was an infrastructure failure before archival, training, scoring, result recording, or budget consumption: a legacy attempt-0098/micro-0001 ref blocked the regular ref. An audit found the same unrecorded legacy pattern through attempt 0200; all 103 commits were atomically preserved under refs/autoresearch/recovered/legacy-* and only their conflicting names plus the empty attempt-0098 directory were removed. Candidate and conditions are unchanged. Hypothesis: attempt-0097 failed because addition requires directed query-to-key compatibility, not because separate Q/K factors or head-specific forms are essential. This major representational change preserves a full asymmetric 16x16 bilinear form, shares it across heads, retains the 16x16 value transform, and yields 1,465 parameters by averaging the checkpoint-derived head forms. It is more informative than a low-rank per-head alternative because it isolates head-specific geometry while restoring every asymmetric interaction removed by the failed symmetric candidate. Generic causal softmax self-attention and autoregressive greedy decoding remain intact.
